text: Finals week is approaching and I have three project submissions due on Friday. I can feel my heart pounding every time I open my laptop.
I couldn't sleep until 4 AM again last night because my mind kept racing about my CGPA.
I feel like no matter how hard I study for Data Structures, my grades never reflect the hours I put in.
All my friends got internship offers at top companies and I haven't even received an interview call. I feel completely left behind.
Why do professors schedule surprise quizzes right after midterm week? It makes zero sense and everyone is furious.
I'm juggling two part-time tutoring jobs to pay for college fees while managing six lab courses. I am completely overwhelmed and burnt out.
My group project partners haven't contributed a single line of code and the submission deadline is tomorrow morning.
I just got accepted for a research conference presentation! All the weekend coding sessions finally paid off.
Today was a productive day. Finished the machine learning assignment and went for a run in the evening.
Just another regular Tuesday attending operating systems lectures and taking notes.
The campus library closes at 8 PM during exam week which is honestly so inconvenient.
I feel lonely in the hostel. Everyone is either studying in their rooms or already in close-knit friend groups.
I have to send my tuition fee invoice tomorrow and I'm stressed about whether the bank education loan will clear in time.
I aced the compiler design viva today, absolutely killed it!
These semester exam papers were brutal, the calculus professor really murdered us with that proof.
I'm dead tired after that 4-hour lab practical, need twelve hours of uninterrupted sleep.
I feel so empty inside. Sitting in class and looking around, I feel completely disconnected from everything.
Can't stop worrying about campus placements next semester. What if I graduate without a job offer?
My parents expect a 9+ CGPA every semester and the constant pressure is suffocating.
Spent the afternoon hanging out with college friends at the canteen, felt so refreshing.
Submitted the software engineering assignment just two minutes before the midnight deadline. My hands were shaking.
Living on instant noodles because money is tight until the end of the month.
I am so proud of my team for winning second place in the 24-hour hackathon!
I feel so hopeless about my academic trajectory. I failed two core modules and don't know how to recover.
The WiFi in the student dormitory hasn't worked for three days straight. How are we supposed to submit assignments?
Read two chapters of computer networks textbook and made flashcards for revision.
I keep procrastinating on my final year capstone project because the scope feels impossibly large.
Woke up with an overwhelming sense of dread today. I couldn't bring myself to attend morning classes.
My mentor gave me fantastic feedback on my deep learning thesis proposal today!
I haven't eaten a proper meal in two days because I've been glued to my desk preparing for competitive coding rounds.
Every time someone on LinkedIn posts their Google internship offer I feel a wave of panic.
Nobody in my class talks to me unless they need my lab assignment code to copy.
Had a calm morning coffee and revised my notes for the upcoming presentation.
I'm terrified of public speaking and tomorrow I have to present my seminar to eighty students and faculty.
Finally understood Dijkstra's algorithm after struggling with it all week. Such a satisfying feeling!
College feels like an endless conveyor belt of quizzes, midterms, labs, and end-sems with no room to breathe.
My scholarship was delayed and now the admin department is charging late registration fees. This is ridiculous.
I just want to crawl into bed and sleep for a week. Everything takes so much energy.
Working out at the university gymnasium every morning has really improved my focus and stamina.
The attendance policy requiring 75% mandatory presence even when sick is completely unfair.
Reviewed the DBMS syllabus and downloaded previous years question papers from the portal.
I don't know who I am anymore outside of being an engineering student chasing numbers.
Got rejected after the final HR round of my dream company. It hurts so much after four rounds of coding.
My roommate snores and plays games with the lights on until 3 AM. I am constantly sleep deprived.
We built a working prototype for our IoT project and the sensors are calibrating smoothly!
I keep checking my email every five minutes waiting for the scholarship decision notification.
Feeling completely burned out. I have zero motivation left to finish this semester.
Had a wholesome phone call with my mom today, she reminded me that my grades don't define my worth.
The lab assistant deducted marks from my submission because I used Python 3.11 instead of 3.8.
Attended the guest lecture on distributed systems. It was informative and well-structured.
I feel like an imposter in my AI class. Everyone else seems to understand backpropagation intuitively.
I spent the entire weekend crying in my room because I feel like a disappointment to my family.
I'm so exhausted that I fell asleep during the afternoon signal processing lecture.
Celebrated my birthday with my hostel mates tonight. They surprised me with a cake at midnight!
Can't concentrate on my books for more than ten minutes. My brain feels foggy and sluggish.
I have no financial safety net. If I don't get placed this semester, I don't know how I will repay my family debts.
The university mess food has been terrible lately and giving several students stomach issues.
Organized my study desk and planned out my revision timetable for the upcoming month.
I killed that mock interview today! The interviewer said my problem solving approach was top notch.
My parents compared my CGPA to my cousin who scored 9.8. I am so tired of this toxic comparison.
I have three back-to-back lab vivas tomorrow and haven't started preparing for the second one.
Nobody noticed that I was absent from college for four straight days. I am invisible.
Completed the cloud computing certification exam on my first attempt!
My computer crashed in the middle of writing my 20-page seminar report without saving.
Walking across the campus green in the evening breeze helped clear my cluttered thoughts.
Everything feels heavy and meaningless lately. I struggle to find any excitement in things I used to love.
I have an exam in two hours and my stomach is in knots. I can barely keep water down.
Packed my bags for the weekend trip home after completing the mid-semester evaluations.
Managing college attendance while dealing with chronic back pain from studying is exhausting.
Our professor complimented our natural language processing project during lab demonstration today.
I feel paralyzed whenever I sit down to study. The backlog of topics is just too massive.
I feel discarded by my old friend group after we got assigned to different section batches.
Why does the hostel warden enforce a 7 PM curfew on female students when male students have no curfew?
Helped my classmate debug their segmentation fault error in C++. Felt good to solve it together.
Just printed my hall ticket and checked the examination seat allotment notice.
I'm so stressed about my family's financial situation that I can't focus during classes.
I have lost over five kilograms this semester because I forget to eat meals during project sprints.
Getting eight full hours of restful sleep made me feel like an entirely new person today.
The campus placement cell canceled our interview slot with no prior warning or explanation.
I feel like I'm drowning in coursework while pretending to be fine in front of everyone.
I am trembling before this technical interview. Imposter syndrome is at an all-time high.
Shared notes with my study group over chai at the college gate.
I spent three hours waiting in line at the scholarship accounts office only to be told to come back Monday.
Attended five hours of lecture, had lunch, and finished the tutorial problem set.
I have no energy to socialize, reply to WhatsApp messages, or even step out of my hostel room.
My heart won't stop racing. I feel like something terrible is about to happen even when nothing is wrong.
I finally deployed our full-stack web application to AWS and the API endpoints are responding in under 50ms!
I hate having to ask my parents for pocket money when I know they are already struggling financially.
Studied operating system memory management concepts and solved numerical problems on paging.
I'm terrified that I will disappoint everyone who believed in me.
The lab air conditioning has been broken for two weeks and it is 38 degrees inside.
Went for an evening walk around the football ground with my roommate and talked about our future dreams.
I feel numb. I received my semester grades and I couldn't even bring myself to feel happy or sad.
I have so many assignments due that I haven't showered or stepped outside in two days.
Successfully submitted our paper abstract to the IEEE student conference!
I have panic attacks every Sunday evening thinking about facing the upcoming college week.
My group members submitted plagiarized code and now the entire team is facing academic disciplinary action.
Wrote down my weekly goals in my journal and prioritized high-impact tasks.
I feel like everyone else has their life sorted out with clear career paths, while I am completely lost.
I drank four cups of black coffee to pull an all-nighter for the compiler design lab exam.
